items.title: AMDockVS
items.text:
AMDockVS is the next-generation version of Assisted Molecular Docking (AMDock), published in 2020. The new version is a desktop application and Python API that includes molecular import, preparation, QSAR, binding-site analysis, docking, and result inspection.

Cite AMDock

The original AMDock paper was published in Biology Direct and is available here. If you use AMDock, please cite it as follows:

Valdés-Tresanco, M.S., Valdés-Tresanco, M.E., Valiente, P.A. et al. AMDock: a versatile graphical tool for assisting molecular docking with Autodock Vina and Autodock4. Biology Direct 15, 12 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1186/s13062-020-00267-2

items.title: Install
items.text:
AMDockVS installs into a conda environment (micromamba or conda). The compiled scientific stack comes from conda-forge, with builds for Linux and macOS on both Intel and ARM; AMDockVS, PySide6, PyMOL (the pymol-open-source 3.2 wheels) and the MolSuite packages come from PyPI:

curl -LO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AMDockVS/AMDockVS/main/environment.yml
micromamba create -n amdockvs -f environment.yml   # or: conda env create -f environment.yml
micromamba activate amdockvs

Do not conda install into that environment afterwards; edit environment.yml and create it again instead.

Start the desktop application with:

amdockvs

items.title: AMDockVS in a nutshell
items.text:
AMDockVS brings molecular preparation, virtual screening, and analysis into a single project workspace. It builds on the original AMDock's goal of making docking accessible, adding tools to organize compound libraries, explore chemical diversity, and work with experimental activity data. Each project keeps the molecules, settings, calculations, and results of a study together.

Docking Studio guides you through program selection, ligand and receptor preparation, search-space setup, and launching a run. Supported docking programs include AutoDock Vina, QuickVina 2, gnina, AutoDock-GPU, and Uni-Dock. You can define a search box manually or use Pocket Detection to identify candidate binding sites with P2Rank.

The surrounding tools help you shape the study before docking. Build prepares molecular structures, Filter applies property criteria, and Diversity groups similar compounds so you can choose representatives. When measured activities are available, QSAR provides a workflow for training and evaluating regression and classification models.

Results connect numerical scores with structural inspection: selecting a docking pose displays its complex in PyMOL, while 2D Interactions maps its protein–ligand contacts. Calculations run in the background and can be followed in the Jobs monitor. The Python API also exposes the project's workflows for scripting, automation, and integration with other analysis tools.

items.title: Main analysis tools
items.text: AMDockVS has two main analysis tools: Docking Studio for preparing, configuring and launching docking runs, and QSAR for training models and scoring molecules. Each guide follows the corresponding workspace panels and describes their controls.

items.title: Docking Studio
items.text: Use Docking Studio to choose docking programs, prepare ligands and receptors, review the docking scope, and launch runs. See the Docking Studio guide for the step-by-step workflow.

items.title: QSAR
items.text: Use QSAR to build models from activity data, predict activities for project ligands or screening shards, and review model results. See the QSAR guide for model building, prediction and analysis.

submit_job(job, *, params: Any = None, executor_name: Optional[str] = None, cpu_required: Optional[int] = None, max_job_cpu: Optional[int] = None, max_inflight_tasks: Optional[int] = None, total_chunks: Optional[int] = None, depends_on: Optional[list[str]] = None, priority: int = 0, result_handler_kwargs: Optional[dict] = None, auto_depends: bool = True) -> str

Submit a job, auto-waiting for active prerequisite jobs by default.

With auto_depends=True (default) the job is held until every active job of its prerequisite categories finishes, so a deferred pipeline can be queued at once. Pass auto_depends=False to submit immediately regardless of running jobs. Returns the key of the job in the project's journal, which is its id everywhere here.

def submit_job(
    self,
    job,
    *,
    params: Any = None,
    executor_name: Optional[str] = None,
    cpu_required: Optional[int] = None,
    max_job_cpu: Optional[int] = None,
    max_inflight_tasks: Optional[int] = None,
    total_chunks: Optional[int] = None,
    depends_on: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    priority: int = 0,
    result_handler_kwargs: Optional[dict] = None,
    auto_depends: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Submit a job, auto-waiting for active prerequisite jobs by default.

    With auto_depends=True (default) the job is held until every active job of its
    prerequisite categories finishes, so a deferred pipeline can be queued at once.
    Pass auto_depends=False to submit immediately regardless of running jobs.
    Returns the key of the job in the project's journal, which is its id everywhere here.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    depends_on = list(depends_on or [])
    depends_on += [job_id for job_id in getattr(self, "_forced_dependencies", None) or () if job_id not in depends_on]
    if auto_depends:
        depends_on = self.resolve_job_dependencies(job, depends_on) or []
    workspace = self.workspace
    job_config = self._job_config()
    engine_job, on_error = job.engine_job(handler_kwargs=result_handler_kwargs)
    job_params = job.validate_params(params)
    total = total_chunks if total_chunks is not None else job.count_chunks(job_params, config=job_config)
    job_id = uuid4().hex
    engine_ids = self._engine_ids()
    executor = self._run_on(job, executor_name)
    engine_ids[job_id] = workspace.submit(
        engine_job,
        job_params,
        key=job_id,
        executor=executor,
        **self._asks(executor),
        # A job that ended in an earlier session has nothing left to wait for.
        after=[engine_ids[dep] for dep in depends_on if dep in engine_ids],
        total=total,
        cpu=cpu_required,
        window=max_inflight_tasks,
        max_cpu=max_job_cpu,
        priority=priority,
        on_error=on_error,
        **({"thread": True} if job.on_thread is not None and job.on_thread(job_params) else {}),
    )
    # Single funnel for "a job just started" UI feedback (the main window plugs a toast in
    # here). May fire from a worker thread, so the hook must be thread-safe (a Qt signal).
    hook = getattr(self, "on_job_submitted", None)
    if hook is not None:
        try:
            hook(str(getattr(job, "name", "") or "Job"), job_id)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - feedback must never break a submit
            pass
    return job_id

def submit_campaign(self, job, *, params: Any, executor_name: str, priority: int = 0) -> str:
    """Submit an `ms_flow.campaign` to the queue `executor_name`; its key in the journal is
    its identity, so the same campaign submitted again is the job that already follows it.

    ponytail: its elements are made now, from what the project has now: it waits for no job.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    self._job_config()  # what its source and writer read of the project
    engine_id = self.workspace.submit(job, params, executor=executor_name, priority=priority,
                                      **self._asks(executor_name))
    job_id = str(self.workspace.engine.status(engine_id).key)
    self._engine_ids()[job_id] = engine_id
    hook = getattr(self, "on_job_submitted", None)
    if hook is not None:
        try:
            hook(str(job.__job__["name"]), job_id)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - feedback must never break a submit
            pass
    return job_id

def job_destinations(self, job_id: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """`run_destinations` for a job on record: where it may be continued now. Nowhere for one
    that cannot be submitted again; a campaign, only to an active queue."""

        job, was_on = self._recorded_job(job_id)
        if job is None:
            return [(name, label) for name, label in self.run_destinations() if self.is_queue(name)]
        return self.run_destinations(job)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - not on record, or its declaration is gone
        return []

Continue a job that was canceled or interrupted, on executor_name or where it was.

A job that is still running is canceled first and waited for, which is how it is moved to another executor: not from a thread that cannot wait. It waits for the jobs its kind waits for, as when it was submitted.

def resume_job(self, job_id: str, executor_name: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Continue a job that was canceled or interrupted, on `executor_name` or where it was.

    A job that is still running is canceled first and waited for, which is how it is moved
    to another executor: not from a thread that cannot wait. It waits for the jobs its kind
    waits for, as when it was submitted.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    job_id = str(job_id)
    job, was_on = self._recorded_job(job_id)
    if job is None:  # a campaign: back to its queue, where what it has there is found again by its key
        executor = executor_name or was_on
        if not self.is_queue(executor):
            raise ValueError(f"a campaign goes to a cluster's queue, and `{executor}` is not one")
        self._job_config()  # what its writer and its end read of the project
        self._engine_ids()[job_id] = self.workspace.move(job_id, executor, **self._asks(executor))
        return job_id
    executor = self._run_on(job, executor_name or was_on)
    if job.name == "amdock_docking_job" and self.is_queue(executor):
        return self.docking.move_to_queue(job_id, executor)  # one job of the queue, not a task per chunk
    self._job_config()
    engine_ids = self._engine_ids()
    waits = [engine_ids[dep] for dep in self.resolve_job_dependencies(job) or ()
             if dep in engine_ids and dep != job_id]
    engine_ids[job_id] = self.workspace.move(job_id, executor, after=waits)
    return job_id

def resolve_job_dependencies(self, job, explicit: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> Optional[list[str]]:
    """Union of explicit depends_on and the ids of active jobs this one should wait for."""
    category = _job_category(getattr(job, "name", "") or "")
    prereqs = _JOB_PREREQS.get(category or "", ())
    deps: list[str] = list(explicit or [])
    if prereqs or category == "chemistry":
        for status in self.list_jobs(statuses=NON_TERMINAL_JOB_STATUSES):
            active_category = _job_category(status.task_type)
            serial_chemistry = category == "chemistry" and active_category == "chemistry"
            if (active_category in prereqs or serial_chemistry) and status.job_id not in deps:
                deps.append(status.job_id)
    return deps or None

def wait_for_job(self, job_id: str, *, poll_s: float = 0.2) -> JobStatus:
    """Block until the job has ended. `poll_s` is not used: the engine tells."""
    self._require_active_project()
    engine_id = self._engine_ids().get(str(job_id))
    if engine_id is None:  # of an earlier session: it ended with it
        status = self.get_job_status(job_id)
        if status is None:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown job: {job_id}")
        return status
    return self._job_status_from_snapshot(self.workspace.engine.wait(engine_id))

def watch_jobs(self, job_ids: Iterable[str], *, poll_s: float = 0.2) -> dict[str, JobStatus]:
    """Display concurrent tqdm progress for several jobs of this session."""
    self._require_active_project()
    from ms_flow.progress import watch_jobs

    job_ids = [str(item) for item in job_ids]
    engine_ids = self._engine_ids()
    snapshots = watch_jobs(self.workspace.engine, [engine_ids[job_id] for job_id in job_ids], poll_s=poll_s)
    return {job_id: self._job_status_from_snapshot(snapshots[engine_ids[job_id]]) for job_id in job_ids}

def run_destinations(self, job=None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Where a job may be sent now, as (executor_name, label): the executors that are
    active, the default one first. With `job`, only the ones that job can run on.
    """
    self._require_active_project()
    rows = [row for row in self.workspace.executors() if row["state"] == "on"]
    # ponytail: `hpc` in the old list of a job is what says its worker needs nothing of
    # this machine but its payload and the files marked in it; one flag when the lists go.
    if job is not None and "hpc" not in job.supported_executors:
        rows = [row for row in rows if row["hosts"] == ["local"]]
    return [(row["name"], row["name"]) for row in sorted(rows, key=lambda row: not row["default"])]

def excluded_since(self, before: set[int], *, limit: int = 10_000) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
    """``(id, name, reason)`` of the molecules excluded now but not in ``before`` — what a run
    failed. ponytail: a run alongside it mixes its failures in; per-job ids if that matters."""
    new = sorted(self.excluded_ids() - set(before))[: int(limit)]
    if not new:
        return []
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = session.exec(
            select(MoleculeRecord.id, MoleculeRecord.name, MoleculeRecord.exclusion_reason)
            .where(MoleculeRecord.id.in_(new))
            .order_by(MoleculeRecord.id)
        ).all()
    return [(int(i), str(name or ""), str(reason or "")) for i, name, reason in rows]

def details(self, molecule_id: int) -> Details | None:
    """Load the complete Details-panel projection for a molecule."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    resolved_id = int(molecule_id)
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        molecule = session.get(MoleculeRecord, resolved_id)
        if molecule is None:
            return None
        binding_sites = tuple(session.exec(
            select(BindingSite)
            .where(BindingSite.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(BindingSite.id)
        ).all())
        receptor_complexes = tuple(session.exec(
            select(ComplexRecord)
            .where(ComplexRecord.receptor_molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(ComplexRecord.id.desc())
        ).all())
        ligand_complexes = tuple(session.exec(
            select(ComplexRecord)
            .where(ComplexRecord.ligand_molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(ComplexRecord.id.desc())
        ).all())
        activities = tuple(session.exec(
            select(LigandActivity)
            .where(LigandActivity.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .order_by(LigandActivity.id.desc())
        ).all())
        structure = molecule_payload_id(molecule)
        current_model = None if structure is None else session.exec(
            select(MoleculeModel)
            .where(MoleculeModel.molecule_id == resolved_id)
            .where(MoleculeModel.payload_id == int(structure))
            .order_by(MoleculeModel.id.desc())
        ).first()
        plddt_model = current_model
        if current_model is None or current_model.source != ModelSource.ESMFOLD:
            plddt_model = session.exec(
                select(MoleculeModel)
                .where(MoleculeModel.molecule_id == resolved_id)
                .where(MoleculeModel.source == ModelSource.ESMFOLD)
                .where(MoleculeModel.payload_id.is_not(None))
                .order_by(MoleculeModel.id.desc())
            ).first()

    def model_data(model):
        if model is None or model.data_payload_id is None:
            return None
        import json

        from amdockvs.core.payloads import read_structure

        data = json.loads(read_structure(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, model.data_payload_id)[0])
        data.pop("pae", None)
        return data

    current_data = model_data(current_model)
    return self.Details(
        molecule=molecule,
        binding_sites=binding_sites,
        receptor_complexes=receptor_complexes,
        ligand_complexes=ligand_complexes,
        activities=activities,
        current_model=current_model,
        current_model_data=current_data,
        plddt_model=plddt_model,
        plddt_model_data=current_data if plddt_model is current_model else model_data(plddt_model),
    )

def apply_filter(
    self,
    scope: MoleculeScope | Selection[Any],
    criteria,
    *,
    action: str,
    reason: str = "",
    exclusion_reason_prefix: str = "",
    set_name: str = "",
) -> tuple[int, int | None]:
    """Apply an evaluated filter or persist its matches as a molecule set."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from amdockvs.molecules import filtering as filter_sql

    normalized_action = str(action or "").strip().lower()
    if normalized_action not in {"enrich", "recover", "tag"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported molecule-filter action: {action!r}")
    conditions = filter_sql.scope_conditions(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, as_molecule_scope(scope))
    prefix = str(exclusion_reason_prefix or "").strip()
    if prefix:
        conditions.append(MoleculeRecord.exclusion_reason.like(f"{prefix}%"))
    if normalized_action == "tag":
        ids = filter_sql.matched_ids(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, conditions, criteria)
        ref = self.create_set(
            ids,
            name=set_name,
            kind="filter",
            metadata={"source": str(reason or "")},
        )
        return len(ids), int(ref.id)
    return filter_sql.apply_state(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        conditions,
        criteria,
        activate_matches=normalized_action == "recover",
        exclude_nonmatches=normalized_action == "enrich",
        reason=str(reason or ""),
    )

def edit(self, molecule_id: int, molblock: str, *, copy: bool = False) -> int | None:
    """Give a molecule an edited structure (a molfile from the 2D editor).

    `copy=False` replaces it: everything computed from the old structure goes (`clear_derived`:
    conformers, engine preparations, descriptors, fingerprints, docking results...) and so do its
    activities, measured on the old compound; the imported original (stored_payload_id), sets and
    complexes stay. `copy=True` leaves the molecule alone and adds the edit as a new one, with
    nothing of the old one's but its role. Returns the id holding the edit, or None when the
    drawing is still the same compound, which changes nothing."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from sqlalchemy import delete as sql_delete

    from amdockvs.chemistry.structures import molecule_mol, sdf_payload
    from amdockvs.core.payloads import payload_store
    from amdockvs.io.rows import identity_representations, structure_fields
    from amdockvs.models.qsar import LigandActivity
    from amdockvs.molecules.editing import edited_structure
    from amdockvs.project.deletion import clear_derived

    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    molecule = self.get(molecule_id)
    if molecule is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
    mol = edited_structure(molblock, molecule_mol(project_db, molecule))
    if mol is None:
        return None
    fields = structure_fields(mol)
    identity = {key: fields.pop(key) for key in ("inchikey", "canonical_smiles")}
    store = payload_store(project_db)
    if not copy:
        clear_derived(project_db, [molecule.id])
    with project_db.get_session() as session:
        edited_payload, = store.put(session, [sdf_payload(mol)])
        if copy:
            parent = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
            row = MoleculeRecord(**parent.model_dump(exclude={"id", "ro5_violations"}))
            row.name = f"{parent.name} (edited)"
            row.stored_payload_id = edited_payload  # the edit is all this molecule ever had
            row.in_set = False
            metadata = {"edited_from": int(parent.id)}
            replaced = None
        else:
            session.exec(sql_delete(LigandActivity).where(LigandActivity.molecule_id == int(molecule.id)))
            row = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
            metadata = sanitize_molecule_extra_data(row.extra_data)
            for stale in ("chemistry", "history", "state"):  # described the structure that is gone
                metadata.pop(stale, None)
            replaced = row.current_payload_id
        row.current_payload_id = edited_payload
        for key, value in fields.items():
            setattr(row, key, value)
        row.is_minimized = False
        metadata["edited"] = True
        row.extra_data = metadata
        session.add(row)
        session.flush()
        for representation in identity_representations(identity, molecule_id=int(row.id)):
            session.merge(MoleculeRepresentation(**representation))
        session.commit()
        edited_id = int(row.id)
    if replaced:
        store.release([replaced])  # an earlier edit's bytes; the import is still referenced, so it stays
    return edited_id

def select_fragment(self, molecule_id: int, fragment_index: int) -> Any:
    """Make another component of the imported original the molecule's current structure.

    Fragments are not stored: this one is cut again from the original and written alone. What
    was computed from the old structure goes (`clear_derived`); activities, measured on the
    imported compound, stay."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    from amdockvs.chemistry.structures import molecule_mol, sdf_payload
    from amdockvs.core.payloads import payload_store
    from amdockvs.io.rows import identity_representations, structure_fields
    from amdockvs.molecules.fragments import fragments_of
    from amdockvs.project.deletion import clear_derived

    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    molecule = self.get(molecule_id)
    if molecule is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
    original = molecule_mol(project_db, {"stored_payload_id": molecule.stored_payload_id})
    if original is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} has no imported original to take a fragment from.")
    fragment = fragments_of(original).get(int(fragment_index))
    if fragment is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Fragment {fragment_index} does not exist for molecule {molecule_id}.")
    store = payload_store(project_db)
    clear_derived(project_db, [molecule.id])
    with project_db.get_session() as session:
        fragment_payload, = store.put(session, [sdf_payload(fragment)])
        row = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule.id))
        replaced = row.current_payload_id
        metadata = sanitize_molecule_extra_data(row.extra_data)
        if isinstance(metadata.get("fragmentation"), dict):  # a copy: in place, the JSON column sees no change
            metadata["fragmentation"] = {**metadata["fragmentation"], "selected_fragment_index": int(fragment_index)}
        for stale in ("chemistry", "history", "state"):  # described the structure that is gone
            metadata.pop(stale, None)
        row.extra_data = metadata
        row.current_payload_id = fragment_payload
        row.is_minimized = False
        fields = structure_fields(fragment)
        identity = {key: fields.pop(key) for key in ("inchikey", "canonical_smiles")}
        for key, value in fields.items():
            setattr(row, key, value)
        session.add(row)
        for representation in identity_representations(identity, molecule_id=int(row.id)):
            session.merge(MoleculeRepresentation(**representation))
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(row)
    if replaced:
        store.release([replaced])  # a no-op while it is still the import or a model's
    return row

def shard_ligands(
    self,
    files: Iterable[PathLike],
    *,
    shard_size: int | None = None,
    executor_name: str = "compute",
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    molecule_kind: str = "small_molecule",
    prefilter: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    temporary_files: Iterable[PathLike] | None = None,
    force: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """The `htpvs` import: split the library into shards, materialize nothing.

    Same feed as `load_ligands` — the byte-span splitter — with the record cap read as
    shard size. What changes is the worker: it writes the span back out as a file and
    registers a `screening_shards` row instead of parsing molecules into the project db.
    """
    normalized_files = normalize_files(files, label="ligand files")
    if not normalized_files:
        return []
    records = (
        default_shard_size(runtime=self.runtime)
        if shard_size is None
        else int(shard_size)
    )
    records = max(1, min(records, MAX_SHARD_RECORDS))
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "file_paths": [str(file_path) for file_path in normalized_files],
        **self._temporary(normalized_files, temporary_files),
        "batch_size": records,
        "molecule_kind": str(molecule_kind or "small_molecule"),
        **self._batches(normalized_files, force=force, kind=ImportKind.SHARDS, role="ligand"),
    }
    if prefilter:
        params["prefilter"] = dict(prefilter)
    return [
        self._submit_job(
            shard_ligands_job,
            params=params,
            executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on,
            # ramp=False, like the feed: an over-declared total never completes.
            total_chunks=_total_import_chunks(normalized_files, batch_size=records, ramp=False),
            max_inflight_tasks=import_max_inflight(self.runtime),
            # The queue that cuts the shards lives here, in the parent: it needs the
            # project's shard directory and its database, neither of which a job spec
            # knows at declaration time.

def run_ligand_pipeline(
    self,
    steps: Sequence[str | tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]],
    *,
    ligands: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    structure_source: str = "current",
    batch_size: int = 128,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """Run several chemistry steps in one pass over the active screening library.

    `run_ligand_pipeline(["standardize", "protonate", "generate_3d"])` reads and writes every
    ligand once; the three single-step jobs read and rewrite the whole library three times.

    With no explicit row scope, a sharded library dispatches whole shards automatically.
    Passing ``ligands`` always selects the row adapter for curated/reference molecules.

    ponytail: the single-step methods below validate their own arguments (pH range, method
    names, tool installs). Here the step params go through as given and the worker raises.
    """
    normalized = normalize_steps(steps)
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("run_ligand_pipeline needs at least one step.")
    for name, _params in normalized:
        if name not in LIGAND_STEPS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ligand chemistry operation: {name}")
    normalized = [
        (name, self._protonate_params(**params) if name == "protonate" else params)
        for name, params in normalized
    ]
    if ligands is None:
        self.runtime._require_active_project()
        if has_shards(self.runtime.workspace.project_db):
            return self.run_shard_pipeline(
                normalized,
                executor_name=executor_name,
                depends_on=depends_on,
                wait=wait,
            )
    return self._submit_ligand_operation(
        [[name, params] for name, params in normalized],
        ligands=ligands,
        params={},
        structure_source=structure_source,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        wait=wait,
    )

def run_shard_pipeline(
    self,
    steps: Sequence[str | tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]],
    *,
    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """The same steps as `run_ligand_pipeline`, over the shards of an `htpvs` project.

    One shard per chunk, one file in and one file out. The run writes into a new
    generation and only switches to it if it finishes, so a crashed run changes nothing
    and the retry simply starts over from the generation that is still the library.
    """
    normalized = normalize_steps(steps)
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("run_shard_pipeline needs at least one step.")
    for name, _params in normalized:
        if name not in LIGAND_STEPS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported ligand chemistry operation: {name}")
    normalized = [
        (name, self._protonate_params(**params) if name == "protonate" else params)
        for name, params in normalized
    ]
    if any(name == "conformers" for name, _params in normalized):
        raise ValueError(
            "Sharded conformer ensembles are not supported: one shard record currently "
            "stores one molecular structure. Generate conformers after materialization."
        )
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    # Opened here, before anything runs: the feed needs its output directory and the
    # result handler needs its id, and neither can invent one of its own without the two
    # disagreeing about where the generation lives.
    label = "+".join(name for name, _ in normalized)
    shards_root = Path(self.runtime.get_project_resource_path(RESOURCE_SHARDS))
    generation_id = create_generation(project_db, step=label, shard_dir=shards_root)
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        shard_chemistry_job,
        params=ShardChemistryJobParams(
            operation=[[name, step_params] for name, step_params in normalized],
            params=dict(params or {}),
            generation_id=generation_id,
            output_dir=str(shards_root / f"gen_{generation_id:04d}_{label}"),
        ).model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY,
        result_handler_kwargs={"project_db": project_db, "generation_id": generation_id},
    )
    return self.runtime.wait_for_job(job_id) if wait else job_id

def predict_receptors(
        self,
        *,
        receptors: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        model: str = FAST_MODEL,
        force: bool = False,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        wait: bool = False,
) -> str | JobStatus:
    """Predict protein structures from sequence with the ESMFold API (thread executor).

    Only proteins without 3D by default; `force=True` predicts again and points the current structure
    to the new model. The token comes from ESM_API_KEY and is never stored.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    if not api_token():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{ESM_TOKEN_ENV} is not set: paste your Biohub API token first.")
    receptor_set_ref = None if receptors is None or is_molecule_scope(receptors) else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, receptors, name="chemistry_receptor_predict_input")
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptors) if is_molecule_scope(receptors) else {}
    receptor_filters = dict(receptor_scope.get("filters") or {})
    if "molecule_type" not in receptor_filters:
        receptor_filters["is_receptor"] = True
    if receptor_scope.get("limit") is not None:
        receptor_filters["_limit"] = receptor_scope.get("limit")
    params = ReceptorPredictionJobParams(
        model=model,
        force=bool(force),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters if force else {**receptor_filters, "has_3d": False},
    )
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    total_items = db_count(project_db, prediction_scope_spec(params))
    # An empty scope with proteins in it means they all have 3D already. An empty scope with
    # no proteins at all may be an import still running: submit and let the job wait for it.
    if total_items == 0 and not force and db_count(project_db, prediction_scope_spec(params.model_copy(update={"receptor_filters": receptor_filters}))):
        raise ValueError("Every protein in scope already has a 3D structure; tick Force to predict again.")
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        receptor_prediction_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name="thread",
        depends_on=depends_on,
        total_chunks=total_items or None,
    )
    if wait:
        return self.runtime.wait_for_job(job_id)
    return job_id

def compute_descriptors(
    self,
    *,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
    only_missing: bool = True,
    batch_size: int = 1000,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    compute_fingerprints: bool = False,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    alerts: bool = False,
    rdkit2d: bool = False,
    molecule_ids: list[int] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Submit the descriptor job. only_missing=True skips ligands that already have
    descriptors computed (MoleculeRecord.mw populated). With compute_fingerprints=True it
    also stores a Morgan fingerprint per ligand, and only_missing then means "lacks that
    fingerprint" so FPs can be added to already-described ligands. rdkit2d=True also stores
    the full RDKit 2D block the models train on (only_missing: lacks that block). With
    alerts=True it is the alerts job instead: PAINS and identity keys, which a library import
    leaves out. molecule_ids narrows the scope to those molecules."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    molecule_set_ref = (
        None
        if molecule_set is None or is_molecule_scope(molecule_set)
        else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, molecule_set, name="qsar_descriptor_input")
    )
    molecule_scope = scope_payload(molecule_set) if is_molecule_scope(molecule_set) else {}
    filters = apply_workflow_filters(
        {**dict(molecule_scope.get("filters") or {}), "excluded": False},
        workflow=QSAR_WORKFLOW,
        role="ligand",
    )
    params = DescriptorJobParams(
        batch_size=batch_size,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set_ref is None else int(molecule_set_ref.id),
        molecule_filters=filters,
        only_missing=bool(only_missing),
        compute_fingerprints=bool(compute_fingerprints),
        fp_radius=int(fp_radius),
        fp_nbits=int(fp_nbits),
        alerts=bool(alerts),
        rdkit2d=bool(rdkit2d),
        molecule_ids=None if molecule_ids is None else [int(i) for i in molecule_ids],
    )
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        calculate_molecule_alerts_job if alerts else calculate_molecule_descriptors_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
    )

def save_site(
        self,
        *,
        molecule_id: int,
        name: str = "",
        source: str = "manual",
        source_ref: str = "",
        center: tuple[float, float, float],
        size: tuple[float, float, float],
        binding_site_id: int | None = None,
        set_active: bool = False,
        extra_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> BindingSite:
    """Saves a site. Without `binding_site_id` it creates a new one; with it, rewrites that one."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        molecule = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(molecule_id))
        if molecule is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Molecule {molecule_id} does not exist.")
        site = None if binding_site_id is None else session.get(BindingSite, int(binding_site_id))
        if site is None:
            site = BindingSite(molecule_id=int(molecule_id))
        elif int(site.molecule_id) != int(molecule_id):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Binding site {binding_site_id} belongs to molecule {site.molecule_id}."
            )
        site.name = str(name or "")
        site.source = str(source or "manual")
        site.source_ref = str(source_ref or "")
        site.center_x = float(center[0])
        site.center_y = float(center[1])
        site.center_z = float(center[2])
        site.size_x = float(size[0])
        site.size_y = float(size[1])
        site.size_z = float(size[2])
        site.extra_data = dict(extra_data or {})
        session.add(site)
        session.flush()
        if set_active:
            set_active_site_row(session, int(molecule_id), int(site.id))
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(site)
        return site

def suggest_box_from_ligand(
        self,
        *,
        ligand_id: int,
        scale: float | None = None,
        padding: float | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Auto box from a reference ligand: center = its centroid, size = cubic box
    derived from the ligand's radius of gyration. Returns {center, size, rg}.

    `scale`/`padding` default to the configured geometry (settings > binding_sites)."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        ligand = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(ligand_id))

            raise ValueError(f"Molecule {ligand_id} does not exist.")

    if not coords:
        raise ValueError(f"No atom coordinates found in ligand {ligand_id}.")
    geometry = app_config(self.runtime).binding_sites
    return box_from_coords(
        coords,

        padding=geometry.box_padding if padding is None else float(padding),
        minimum=geometry.box_min_edge,
        maximum=geometry.box_max_edge,

def preparation_summary(
        self,
        scope: MoleculeScope,
        *,
        role_type: str,
        engine: str = "ad4",
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return total/ready/failed preparation counts for a molecule scope."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    normalized_role = str(role_type or "").strip().lower()
    normalized_engine = str(engine or "ad4").strip().lower()
    if normalized_role not in {"ligand", "receptor"}:
        raise ValueError("role_type must be 'ligand' or 'receptor'.")
    # Count each side alone first: a family with no state row of that kind anywhere needs
    # no join with the scope (the common case before the first preparation).
    molecules = self.runtime.molecules
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    flags = {"is_ligand" if normalized_role == "ligand" else "is_receptor": True, "prepared_engine_key": normalized_engine}

    def in_scope(ready: bool) -> int:
        states = prepared_molecules_spec(role_type=normalized_role, engine=normalized_engine, is_ready=ready)
        if not db_count(project_db, states):
            return 0
        return molecules.count(molecules.filter(scope, filters={**flags, "prepared": ready}))

    total = molecules.count(scope)
    return {"total": total, "ready": in_scope(True) if total else 0, "failed": in_scope(False) if total else 0}

def unprepared_molecules_clause(self, *, role_type: str, engines: list[str] | tuple[str, ...]):
    """Opaque SmartTable clause selecting molecules not ready for every engine family."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    role = str(role_type or "").strip().lower()
    if role not in {"ligand", "receptor"}:
        raise ValueError("role_type must be 'ligand' or 'receptor'.")
    normalized_engines = tuple(
        dict.fromkeys(str(value or "").strip().lower() for value in engines if str(value or "").strip()))
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    if any(
        not db_count(project_db, prepared_molecules_spec(role_type=role, engine=engine))
        for engine in normalized_engines
    ):
        return None  # a family nothing is ready for leaves every row in: no anti-join to run
    # NOT IN, not a correlated NOT EXISTS: DuckDB (1 thread, 1 GB) hash-joins the whole
    # table for the latter (4 s and GBs of spill for one page); SQLite is faster with it too.
    model, molecule_column, payload_column = prep_table(role)
    missing = [
        MoleculeRecord.id.not_in(
            select(molecule_column).where(model.family == engine, payload_column.is_not(None))
        )
        for engine in normalized_engines
    ]
    if not missing:
        return None
    return missing[0] if len(missing) == 1 else or_(*missing)

def pairs_per_task(self, program_spec: DockingProgramSpec, batch_size: int | None) -> int:
    """Pairs per docking task. AutoDock-GPU and Uni-Dock dock a task's pairs in one process
    (see their engines), so their tasks never go below `docking.<engine>.batch_size`."""
    config = app_config(self.runtime).docking

def run_shards(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        hit_threshold: float,
        hit_cap: int,
        output_dir: PathLike | None = None,
        exhaustiveness: int = 8,
        num_modes: int = 9,
        box_center: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        box_size: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        scoring_function: str = "vina",
        vina_backend: str = DEFAULT_VINA_BACKEND,
        vina_command: str = DEFAULT_VINA_COMMAND,
        vina_cpu: int = 1,
        seed: int = 0,
        spacing: float = 0.375,
        energy_range: float = 3.0,
        min_rmsd: float = 1.0,
        run_id: str | None = None,
        protocol_metadata: dict | None = None,
        engine_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        skip_existing: bool = True,
        payload: str = PAYLOAD_LIGHT,
        check_required: bool = True,
        selected_from_receptor_id: int | None = None,
        selected_top_n: int | None = None,
        replace_existing: bool = False,
        off_target_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
) -> str:
    """`run` for a sharded library: the campaign, with the gate that makes it end.

    No ligand scope — the library is the inventory of prepared shards. When the run ends, the
    best `hit_cap` ligands per receptor that pass the `hit_threshold` prefilter become rows;
    both are required, not defaulted: a campaign without them writes back everything it
    scored, which is the failure mode `htpvs` exists to prevent. A dependent off-target
    stage sets `selected_from_receptor_id`; its deferred chunker reads that receptor's
    durable Top-N and extracts only those records from the source shards.

    On a cluster's queue (`executor_name` of kind `queue`) the whole of it is one job of the
    queue (`amdockvs.docking.campaign`): with `off_target_set`, the best `hit_cap` of the one
    receptor of `receptor_set` are docked against those receptors there too, and no
    dependent stage is submitted here.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    queue = self.runtime.is_queue(executor_name)
    if off_target_set is not None and not queue:
        raise ValueError("off_target_set is for a cluster's queue; here the off-target stage is its own run "
                         "(selected_from_receptor_id).")
    if queue and (depends_on or selected_from_receptor_id is not None):
        raise ValueError("A campaign on a cluster's queue runs its off-target stage itself: use off_target_set.")
    if selected_top_n is not None and selected_from_receptor_id is None:
        raise ValueError("selected_top_n requires selected_from_receptor_id.")
    if selected_from_receptor_id is not None and not str(run_id or "").strip():
        raise ValueError("Off-target selection requires the reference run_id.")
    if (box_center is None) ^ (box_size is None):
        raise ValueError("docking.run requires both box_center and box_size when either one is provided.")
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    if not program_spec.supports_shards:
        raise ValueError(f"Docking program '{program_spec.key}' does not support sharded libraries.")
    knobs = dict(
        exhaustiveness=exhaustiveness,
        num_modes=num_modes,
        scoring_function=scoring_function,
        vina_backend=vina_backend,
        vina_command=vina_command,
        vina_cpu=vina_cpu,
        seed=seed,
        spacing=spacing,
        energy_range=energy_range,
        min_rmsd=min_rmsd,
    )
    resolved_engine_config = _validated_engine_config(program_spec, engine_config, **knobs)
    protocol_metadata = self.check_protocol(
        program=program_spec.key, engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=replace_existing,
    )
    reset_results = replace_existing and check_protocol_conflict(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec, protocol=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=True,
    )
    if reset_results and selected_from_receptor_id is not None:
        raise ValueError("Changing docking configuration requires rerunning the reference stage before off-target docking.")
    receptor_set_ref = self._set_ref(receptor_set, name="docking_receptor_input")
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    params = DockShardsJobParams(
        output_dir=self._output_dir(output_dir),
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        box_center=box_center,
        box_size=box_size,
        **_engine_fields(resolved_engine_config, knobs),
        run_id=str(run_id or uuid4().hex),
        protocol_metadata=DockingProtocolMetadata.from_mapping(protocol_metadata or {}),
        engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        hit_threshold=float(hit_threshold),
        hit_cap=int(hit_cap),
        selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
        selected_top_n=(int(selected_top_n) if selected_top_n is not None else int(hit_cap)),
        skip_existing=skip_existing,
        check_required=check_required,
    )
    if reset_results:
        if check_required and not depends_on:
            dock_shards_job.count_chunks(
                params.model_dump(mode="python"), config={"project_db": self.runtime.workspace.project_db},
            )
        clear_previous_docking(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec)
    cpu = program_spec.resource_requirements(resolved_engine_config)["cpu_required"]
    if queue:
        off_ref = self._set_ref(off_target_set, name="docking_off_target_input")
        off_scope = scope_payload(off_target_set) if is_molecule_scope(off_target_set) else {}
        campaign_params = DockCampaignParams(
            **params.model_dump(mode="python"),
            off_receptor_set_id=None if off_ref is None else int(off_ref.id),
            off_receptor_filters=self._program_scope_filters(off_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
            if off_target_set is not None else {},
            cpu_required=cpu,
        )
        return self.runtime.submit_campaign(dock_shards_campaign, params=campaign_params.model_dump(mode="python"),
                                            executor_name=executor_name, priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY)
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        dock_shards_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        priority=SHARDS_PRIORITY,
        cpu_required=cpu,
        # The gate lives in the parent, like the shard queue at import: it counts across
        # chunks and it writes molecules, neither of which a worker can do.
        result_handler_kwargs={
            "project_db": self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
            "hit_cap": int(hit_cap),
            "hit_threshold": float(hit_threshold),
            "run_id": params.run_id,
            "engine": params.engine,
            "protocol_hash": str(params.protocol_metadata.hash or ""),
            "payload": str(payload),
            "selected_from_receptor_id": params.selected_from_receptor_id,
        },
    )

def method_misfit_receptor_ids(self, *, method: str) -> list[int]:
    """Receptors whose active box does not fit the docking `method` (methods.py).
    Receptors without a box are not judged: the user still has to define one. The source
    structure is read: preparation keeps its metals."""
    from amdockvs.docking.methods import excludes

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        rows = session.exec(
            select(MoleculeRecord, BindingSite)
            .join(BindingSite, (BindingSite.molecule_id == MoleculeRecord.id) & (BindingSite.is_active == True))  # noqa: E712
            .where(MoleculeRecord.is_receptor == True)  # noqa: E712 - SQL expression
        ).all()
    misfits: list[int] = []
    for receptor, site in rows:
        box = site_payload(site)
        if box is None:
            continue
        with self._receptor_as_pdb(receptor) as readable:  # mmCIF too: the Zn check reads PDB columns
            if readable is not None and excludes(method, readable, box["center"], box["size"]):
                misfits.append(int(receptor.id))
    return misfits

def list_box_residues(self, *, receptor_id: int, engine: str = "vina") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Residues with at least one atom inside the receptor's active binding-site box.

    Candidate set for flexible-residue selection — short because the box filters it.
    Returns [] when there's no active grid or the structure file is unavailable.
    """
    grid = self.get_grid(receptor_id=int(receptor_id), engine=engine)
    if grid is None:
        return []
    center = tuple(float(v) for v in grid.get("center") or [])
    size = tuple(float(v) for v in grid.get("size") or [])
    if len(center) != 3 or len(size) != 3:
        return []
    with self.runtime.workspace.project_db.get_session() as session:
        receptor = session.get(MoleculeRecord, int(receptor_id))
    if receptor is None:
        return []
    try:
        with self._receptor_as_pdb(receptor) as readable_receptor:
            if readable_receptor is None:
                return []
            residues = residues_in_box(
                readable_receptor.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"), center, size
            )
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return []
    return [
        {"key": r.key, "label": r.label, "chain": r.chain, "resname": r.resname, "resnum": r.resnum}
        for r in residues
    ]

def check_receptors(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Receptor-only half of check_required: preparation + grid status, no ligand scan.

    check_required materializes the full ligand set to report missing ligands; that's
    the expensive part. The Receptors step only shows receptor prep/grid status, so this
    skips ligands entirely (receptor sets are small).
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    receptor_set_ref = (
        None
        if receptor_set is None or is_molecule_scope(receptor_set)
        else ensure_molecule_set_ref(self.runtime, receptor_set, name="docking_check_receptor_input")
    )
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    receptor_rows = list_entity_rows(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        entity_kind="receptor",
        engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        filters=receptor_filters,
        fields=("id", "prepared_engine", "grid_engine"),
        order=("id",),
    )
    receptor_ids = [int(row.get("id") or 0) for row in receptor_rows if int(row.get("id") or 0) > 0]
    ready_prepared = {
        int(row.get("id") or 0)
        for row in receptor_rows
        if not program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation or bool(row.get("prepared_engine"))
    }
    ready_grid = {
        int(row.get("id") or 0)
        for row in receptor_rows
        if not program_spec.requires_binding_site or bool(row.get("grid_engine"))
    }
    return {
        "receptor_ids": receptor_ids,
        "missing": {
            "receptors_prepared": [rid for rid in receptor_ids if rid not in ready_prepared],
            "receptor_binding_sites": [rid for rid in receptor_ids if rid not in ready_grid],
        },
        "counts": {
            "receptors_total": len(receptor_rows),
            "receptors_ready": len(ready_prepared),
            "receptor_grids_ready": len(ready_grid),
        },
    }

def run(
        self,
        *,
        program: str = VINA_PROGRAM.key,
        ligands: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | Selection[MoleculeRecord] | int | None = None,
        receptors: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | Selection[MoleculeRecord] | int | None = None,
        ligand_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        receptor_set: MoleculeSetRef | MoleculeScope | int | None = None,
        output_dir: PathLike | None = None,
        batch_size: int | None = None,
        exhaustiveness: int = 8,
        num_modes: int = 9,
        box_center: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        box_size: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
        scoring_function: str = "vina",
        vina_backend: str = DEFAULT_VINA_BACKEND,
        vina_command: str = DEFAULT_VINA_COMMAND,
        vina_cpu: int = 1,
        seed: int = 0,
        spacing: float = 0.375,
        energy_range: float = 3.0,
        min_rmsd: float = 1.0,
        run_id: str | None = None,
        protocol_metadata: dict | None = None,
        engine_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
        check_required: bool = True,
        skip_existing: bool = True,
        compute_interactions: bool = False,
        hit_threshold: float | None = None,
        hit_cap: int = 0,
        payload: str = PAYLOAD_LIGHT,
        selected_from_receptor_id: int | None = None,
        selected_top_n: int | None = None,
        selected_max_score: float | None = None,
        replace_existing: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Run docking over the active library, selecting its row or shard adapter.

    ``hit_threshold``/``hit_cap`` are optional for materialized rows and mandatory for a
    sharded library, where returning every scored molecule would defeat the storage model.
    ``compute_interactions`` finds each pose's interactions in the chunk that docked it.
    An off-target stage sets ``selected_from_receptor_id``/``selected_top_n``: the other
    receptors dock only that receptor's Top-N ligands, read when the job starts — so it
    `depends_on` the target's job. Over rows, ``selected_max_score`` keeps only those at
    or below it (a sharded library uses ``hit_threshold`` for that).
    """
    if selected_top_n is not None and selected_from_receptor_id is None:
        raise ValueError("selected_top_n requires selected_from_receptor_id.")
    if ligands is not None:
        if ligand_set is not None:
            raise ValueError("Pass either ligands or ligand_set, not both.")
        ligand_set = ligands
    if receptors is not None:
        if receptor_set is not None:
            raise ValueError("Pass either receptors or receptor_set, not both.")
        receptor_set = receptors
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    knobs = dict(
        exhaustiveness=exhaustiveness,
        num_modes=num_modes,
        scoring_function=scoring_function,
        vina_backend=vina_backend,
        vina_command=vina_command,
        vina_cpu=vina_cpu,
        seed=seed,
        spacing=spacing,
        energy_range=energy_range,
        min_rmsd=min_rmsd,
    )
    if ligand_set is None and has_shards(self.runtime.workspace.project_db):
        if hit_threshold is None or int(hit_cap) <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "docking.run over a sharded library requires hit_threshold and hit_cap."
            )
        if compute_interactions:
            raise ValueError(
                "compute_interactions is not available during sharded docking; compute "
                "interactions after hits have been materialized."
            )
        return self.run_shards(
            program=program,
            receptor_set=receptor_set,
            hit_threshold=float(hit_threshold),
            hit_cap=int(hit_cap),
            output_dir=output_dir,
            box_center=box_center,
            box_size=box_size,
            **knobs,
            run_id=run_id,
            protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata,
            engine_config=engine_config,
            executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on,
            skip_existing=skip_existing,
            payload=payload,
            check_required=check_required,
            selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
            selected_top_n=selected_top_n,
            replace_existing=replace_existing,
        )
    if selected_from_receptor_id is not None and not selected_top_n:
        raise ValueError("An off-target stage over ligand rows requires selected_top_n.")
    if hit_cap and hit_threshold is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "docking.run needs hit_threshold when hit_cap is set: the threshold is the "
            "scientific criterion, the cap is only what makes the run end."
        )
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(program)
    resolved_engine_config = _validated_engine_config(program_spec, engine_config, **knobs)
    protocol_metadata = self.check_protocol(
        program=program_spec.key, engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=replace_existing,
    )
    reset_results = replace_existing and check_protocol_conflict(
        self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec, protocol=protocol_metadata, replace_existing=True,
    )
    if reset_results and selected_from_receptor_id is not None:
        raise ValueError("Changing docking configuration requires rerunning the reference stage before off-target docking.")
    resolved_batch_size = self.pairs_per_task(program_spec, batch_size)
    ligand_set_ref = self._set_ref(ligand_set, name="docking_ligand_input")
    receptor_set_ref = self._set_ref(receptor_set, name="docking_receptor_input")
    ligand_scope = scope_payload(ligand_set) if is_molecule_scope(ligand_set) else {}
    receptor_scope = scope_payload(receptor_set) if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else {}
    ligand_filters = self._program_scope_filters(ligand_scope, role="ligand", program=program_spec)
    receptor_filters = self._program_scope_filters(receptor_scope, role="receptor", program=program_spec)
    if box_center is None or box_size is None:
        resolved_grid = self._grid_from_receptor_source(
            receptor_set if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else receptor_set_ref,
            engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        )
        if resolved_grid is not None:
            box_center, box_size, knobs["spacing"] = resolved_grid
    if (box_center is None) ^ (box_size is None):
        raise ValueError("docking.run requires both box_center and box_size when either one is provided.")
    # Always resolve counts: they gate readiness (when requested) AND give the true
    # chunk total so progress is computed against the real pair count instead of
    # completed/emitted-so-far (a lazy generator otherwise leaves total_chunks unknown,
    # making progress hover near 50-60% regardless of actual completion).
    requirement_check = self.check_required(
        program=program_spec.key,
        ligand_set=ligand_set if is_molecule_scope(ligand_set) else ligand_set_ref,
        receptor_set=receptor_set if is_molecule_scope(receptor_set) else receptor_set_ref,
    )
    if check_required and not bool(requirement_check.get("ready")):
        raise RuntimeError(_requirements_message(program_spec.key, requirement_check))
    run_counts = dict(requirement_check.get("counts") or {})
    # The docking feed pairs every prepared ligand with every prepared receptor
    # (receptors without a grid still emit a failed-pair chunk), batched by batch_size.
    total_pairs = int(run_counts.get("ligands_ready") or 0) * int(run_counts.get("receptors_ready") or 0)
    if check_required and total_pairs <= 0:
        # Fail early and clearly instead of submitting a job whose feed yields no pairs
        # (which would otherwise complete silently with zero results).
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"docking.run has no valid ligand-receptor pairs to dock for docking.{program_spec.key}: "
            f"counts={run_counts}. Import and prepare at least one ligand and one receptor first."
        )
    # The feed applies skip_existing after resolving the scoped cross-product. Its declared
    # total must use that same filtered count; over-declaring makes Molsuite wait forever for
    # chunks that the feed intentionally never emits.
    pending_pairs = count_pending_docking_pairs(
        project_db=self.runtime.workspace.project_db,
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        ligand_set_id=None if ligand_set_ref is None else int(ligand_set_ref.id),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        ligand_filters=ligand_filters,
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        protocol_metadata=protocol_metadata,
        skip_existing=False if reset_results else skip_existing,
        requires_ligand_preparation=program_spec.requires_ligand_preparation,
        requires_receptor_preparation=program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation,
    )
    # The Top-N does not exist yet when an off-target stage is submitted: declare nothing
    # (a floor of 0) rather than a count that could over-declare and never complete.
    total_chunks = (
        -(-pending_pairs // resolved_batch_size)
        if pending_pairs > 0 and selected_from_receptor_id is None else 0
    )
    params = DockingJobParams(
        output_dir=self._output_dir(output_dir),
        batch_size=resolved_batch_size,
        row_batch_size=batch_size_for("ligand", self.runtime),
        ligand_set_id=None if ligand_set_ref is None else int(ligand_set_ref.id),
        receptor_set_id=None if receptor_set_ref is None else int(receptor_set_ref.id),
        ligand_filters=ligand_filters,
        receptor_filters=receptor_filters,
        engine=program_spec.docking_engine,
        preparation_engine=program_spec.preparation_engine,
        requires_ligand_preparation=program_spec.requires_ligand_preparation,
        requires_receptor_preparation=program_spec.requires_receptor_preparation,
        requires_binding_site=program_spec.requires_binding_site,
        box_center=box_center,
        box_size=box_size,
        **_engine_fields(resolved_engine_config, knobs),
        run_id=str(run_id or uuid4().hex),
        protocol_metadata=dict(protocol_metadata or {}),
        engine_config=resolved_engine_config,
        skip_existing=skip_existing,
        hit_threshold=hit_threshold,
        hit_cap=max(0, int(hit_cap)),
        interactions=bool(compute_interactions),
        selected_from_receptor_id=selected_from_receptor_id,
        selected_top_n=selected_top_n,
        selected_max_score=selected_max_score,
    )
    cpu = program_spec.resource_requirements(resolved_engine_config)["cpu_required"]
    if self.runtime.is_queue(executor_name):
        return self._run_rows_on_queue(params, executor_name=executor_name, cpu=cpu, depends_on=depends_on,
                                       reset_results=reset_results, program_spec=program_spec)
    if reset_results:
        clear_previous_docking(self.runtime.workspace.project_db, program=program_spec)
    job_id = self.runtime.submit_job(
        docking_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        # Each docking chunk runs one engine process that uses `vina_cpu` threads
        # internally, so reserve that many CPU tokens from the pool to avoid
        # oversubscription (pool limits concurrency to floor(cpus / vina_cpu)).
        cpu_required=cpu,
        # Declare the real chunk total so progress = processed/total (not processed/emitted).
        total_chunks=total_chunks,
    )
    return job_id

Continue a docking run over rows on a cluster's queue: it is stopped here (waited for, so not from a thread that cannot wait) and what it has not docked goes there as a run of its own (_run_rows_on_queue), with its run id. The id of that new job.

def move_to_queue(self, job_id: str, executor_name: str) -> str:
    """Continue a docking run over rows on a cluster's queue: it is stopped here (waited for,
    so not from a thread that cannot wait) and what it has not docked goes there as a run of
    its own (`_run_rows_on_queue`), with its run id. The id of that new job."""
    params = DockingJobParams(**self.runtime.workspace.origin(str(job_id))["params"])
    self._check_queue(params)  # before it is stopped here
    engine_id = self.runtime._engine_ids().get(str(job_id))
    if engine_id is not None:
        self.runtime.workspace.engine.cancel(engine_id)
        self.runtime.workspace.engine.wait(engine_id)
    program_spec = self.get_program_spec(params.protocol_metadata.program or params.engine)
    cpu = program_spec.resource_requirements(params.engine_config)["cpu_required"]
    return self._run_rows_on_queue(params.model_copy(update={"skip_existing": True}), executor_name=executor_name,
                                   cpu=cpu, depends_on=None, reset_results=False, program_spec=program_spec)

def compute_diagrams(
        self,
        *,
        result_ids: list[int] | None = None,
        run_id: str = "",
        receptor_id: int | None = None,
        score_lte: float | None = None,
        pose_rank: int | None = 1,
        fmt: str = "png",

        replace_existing: bool = False,
        executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
        depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render 2D interaction diagrams for docking poses as a standalone job.

    Files land next to each pose (see ``diagram.diagram_path_for``); nothing
    is written to the DB, so re-run with ``replace_existing=True`` to refresh.
    """
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    params = DiagramJobParams(
        result_ids=[int(value) for value in (result_ids or []) if int(value) > 0],
        run_id=str(run_id or ""),
        receptor_id=receptor_id,
        score_lte=score_lte,
        pose_rank=pose_rank,
        fmt=str(fmt or "png"),
        chunk_size=max(1, int(chunk_size)),
        replace_existing=bool(replace_existing),
    )
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        diagram_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        depends_on=depends_on,

num_cpus sets the parallelism: >1 runs bblean multiround with that many processes and the job requests exactly that many CPUs (cpu_required) so mf schedules it correctly. When None it is derived from the scope size via plan_cpus.

shards clusters the library's shards instead (the scope arguments do not apply): a fingerprint job packs them shard by shard, the clustering waits for it, and only the representatives become molecule rows; every member stays in the run's sidecar by io.shards.shard_key. def cluster_job(
    self,
    *,
    method: str = "bitbirch",
    threshold: float = 0.65,
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None,
    molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    with_activity: str = "",
    cluster_run_id: str = "",
    num_cpus: int | None = None,
    executor_name: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_CPU_EXECUTOR,
    depends_on: list[str] | None = None,
    shards: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Submit the clustering job over the DB; results land in ``clustering_results``. Returns
    the job id. The run is tagged with ``cluster_run_id`` (auto if blank) — read it back with
    ``list_runs`` / ``get_run`` or persist its centroids with ``save_centroids_as_set``.
    ``with_activity`` (an activity endpoint) narrows the scope to the ligands measured for it.

    Each cluster starts with its ``per_cluster`` centroid-nearest members as representatives;
    ``pick_representatives`` chooses again, by any mode, without clustering again.

    ``num_cpus`` sets the parallelism: >1 runs bblean multiround with that many processes and the
    job **requests exactly that many CPUs** (``cpu_required``) so mf schedules it correctly. When
    None it is derived from the scope size via ``plan_cpus``.

    ``shards`` clusters the library's shards instead (the scope arguments do not apply): a
    fingerprint job packs them shard by shard, the clustering waits for it, and only the
    representatives become molecule rows; every member stays in the run's sidecar by
    ``io.shards.shard_key``. Both jobs run at ``SHARDS_PRIORITY``."""
    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    if num_cpus is None and shards:
        num_cpus = plan_cpus(ShardStore(self.runtime.workspace.project_db).record_count())
    if num_cpus is None:
        num_cpus = plan_cpus(
            self.scope_count(
                molecule_set=molecule_set, molecule_filters=molecule_filters,
                fp_radius=fp_radius, fp_nbits=fp_nbits, with_activity=with_activity,
            )
        )
    num_cpus = max(1, int(num_cpus))
    params = SelectionClusterJobParams(
        batch_size=app_config(self.runtime).diversity.rows_per_task,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        per_cluster=per_cluster,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set is None else int(getattr(molecule_set, "id", molecule_set)),
        molecule_filters=dict(molecule_filters or {}),
        fp_radius=fp_radius,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits,
        with_activity=with_activity,
        cluster_run_id=cluster_run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex,
        num_processes=num_cpus,
        shards=shards,
    )
    priority = {}
    if shards:
        priority = {"priority": SHARDS_PRIORITY}
        depends_on = [self.runtime.submit_job(
            shard_fingerprints_job, params=params.model_dump(mode="python"), executor_name=executor_name,
            depends_on=depends_on, **priority,
        )]
    return self.runtime.submit_job(
        cluster_molecules_job,
        params=params.model_dump(mode="python"),
        executor_name=executor_name,
        cpu_required=num_cpus,
        depends_on=depends_on,
        **priority,
    )

Samples a random sample_limit subset (seeded by seed so each preview draws a fresh subset), skipping exclude_ids (molecules already previewed) so repeated previews cover more of the space. Projects onto basis when given (a prior preview's fitted PCA axes) so runs overlay in one comparable space; otherwise fits a new basis and returns it. Heavy (DB read + PCA); call off the GUI thread. with_activity restricts the scope to ligands measured for that endpoint, as in cluster_job. Cheap re-clustering then uses cluster_loaded.

def load_universe(
    self,
    *,
    molecule_set: MoleculeSetRef | int | None = None,
    molecule_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    fp_radius: int = 2,
    fp_nbits: int = 2048,
    with_activity: str = "",
    sample_limit: int = DEFAULT_SAMPLE_LIMIT,
    seed: int = 0,
    basis: Any = None,
    exclude_ids: Any = None,
) -> UniverseMatrix:
    """Load a scope's fingerprint matrix + 2-D projection for the interactive view. Samples a
    random ``sample_limit`` subset (seeded by ``seed`` so each preview draws a *fresh* subset),
    skipping ``exclude_ids`` (molecules already previewed) so repeated previews cover more of
    the space. Projects onto ``basis`` when given (a prior preview's fitted PCA axes) so runs
    overlay in one comparable space; otherwise fits a new basis and returns it. Heavy (DB read +
    PCA); call off the GUI thread. ``with_activity`` restricts the scope to ligands measured
    for that endpoint, as in ``cluster_job``. Cheap re-clustering then uses ``cluster_loaded``."""
    import random

    from amdockvs.diversity.clustering import fit_project_2d, fp_matrix_from_bitstrings, project_2d_onto

    self.runtime._require_active_project()
    params = SelectionClusterJobParams(
        batch_size=app_config(self.runtime).diversity.rows_per_task,
        molecule_set_id=None if molecule_set is None else int(getattr(molecule_set, "id", molecule_set)),
        molecule_filters=dict(molecule_filters or {}),
        fp_radius=fp_radius,
        fp_nbits=fp_nbits,
        with_activity=with_activity,
    )
    project_db = self.runtime.workspace.project_db
    skip = {int(i) for i in (exclude_ids or ())}
    rows, total, eligible = _reservoir_sample(
        scope_molecule_rows(project_db, params),
        limit=int(sample_limit),
        seed=int(seed),
        skip=skip,
    )
    sampled = eligible > int(sample_limit)
    stored = stored_fingerprints_for_ids(
        project_db, [int(r["id"]) for r in rows], radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits
    )
    ordered_ids: list[int] = []
    bitstrings: list[bytes] = []
    for row in rows:
        mol_id = int(row["id"])
        fp = stored.get(mol_id) or _fingerprint_from_structure(project_db, row, radius=fp_radius, nbits=fp_nbits)
        if fp is None:
            continue
        ordered_ids.append(mol_id)
        bitstrings.append(fp)
    x_matrix = fp_matrix_from_bitstrings(bitstrings)
    if basis is None:
        projection, evr, basis = fit_project_2d(x_matrix)
    else:
        projection, evr = project_2d_onto(x_matrix, basis), list(basis.get("evr") or [0.0, 0.0])
    return UniverseMatrix(
        molecule_ids=ordered_ids,
        x_matrix=x_matrix,
        projection=[[float(x), float(y)] for x, y in projection],
        projection_variance=list(evr),
        total_in_scope=total,
        sampled=sampled,
        basis=basis,
    )

@staticmethod
def cluster_loaded(
    universe: UniverseMatrix,
    *,
    method: str = "bitbirch",
    per_cluster: int = 1,
    **method_params: Any,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    """Cluster an already-loaded ``UniverseMatrix`` — the cheap step that re-runs on every knob
    change without touching the DB. ``method_params`` (threshold, batch_size, ...) go straight to
    the registered method, so each method's own knobs pass through untouched."""
    threshold = float(method_params.get("threshold", 0.65))
    if not universe.molecule_ids:
        return AnalysisResult(
            [], [], [], {"n_clusters": 0, "n_molecules": 0, "clusters": []}, [], [0.0, 0.0],
            method, threshold, universe.total_in_scope, universe.sampled,
        )
    result = cluster_and_select(
        universe.x_matrix, method=method, per_cluster=per_cluster, with_projection=False, **method_params
    )
    rep_ids = [universe.molecule_ids[i] for i in result.representative_indices]
    return AnalysisResult(
        molecule_ids=universe.molecule_ids,
        labels=[int(v) for v in result.labels],
        representative_ids=rep_ids,
        stats=result.stats,
        projection=universe.projection,
        projection_variance=universe.projection_variance,
        method=method,
        threshold=threshold,
        total_in_scope=universe.total_in_scope,
        sampled=universe.sampled,
    )

Every molecule's fingerprint is loaded and clustered (bblean is fast); only the 2-D graph basis is fitted on a random sub-sample and every point projected onto it (cheap), so the plot scales without the full-N SVD. Returns the same mapping as cluster_loaded, over the whole scope. Heavy — call off the GUI thread. Raises if the scope exceeds INLINE_RUN_LIMIT (that needs the parallel job).
